reported.title: E-stop logic inverted
reported.description: estopActive() returns true when D3 reads HIGH, but with INPUT_PULLUP the pin is HIGH when the e-stop is released and LOW when pressed. This makes the contactor drop when the e-stop is clear and energize when pressed — the opposite of the required fail-safe behaviour.

reported.title: Contactor never follows run request
reported.description: Both the runReq and else branches call setContactor(true), so the contactor is always HIGH whenever the e-stop is clear regardless of D6. The run request input is effectively ignored.

reported.title: Trip count increments on release, not press
reported.description: Because estopActive is inverted, tripCount++ fires on the release edge (HIGH transition) rather than when the e-stop is pressed, so trips counts the wrong events.

truth.description: E-stop polarity inverted vs pull-up wiring

exposing_checks.behaviour: D5 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when D3 == 1; LOW when D3 == 0; within 100 ms (Contactor follows e-stop)

judge_input.spec:
- E-stop on D3 with INPUT_PULLUP, active LOW when pressed. Contactor coil on D5. Run request on D6 (pull-up).
- Contactor D5 must drop LOW when e-stop is held (D3 LOW), and run HIGH when e-stop is released.
- React within 100 ms of a settled e-stop level change.
- Settle the e-stop contact for 30 ms before counting a new trip.
- Print `hoist run=<0|1> trips=<n>` every 1100 ms.
- When e-stop is clear, keep the contactor available (HIGH) for hoist motion.
